details:
SKYWATCH 102 – Exploring the Infrared Universe

SKYWATCH 102 is an interactive astronomical data exploration platform developed using observations from NASA's SPHEREx mission. Its goal is to make astronomical archive data easier to access, explore, visualize, and understand.

The application connects to the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA), allowing users to search for SPHEREx observations using celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination) and a search radius. It supports the retrieval and inspection of astronomical FITS files, observation metadata, and scientific image data.

Users can explore astronomical image cutouts and compare observations captured at different times. Image alignment and blink-animation capabilities help visualize differences between observations and make scientific data more intuitive to investigate.

The project was developed primarily with Python and Streamlit. Its technology stack includes Astropy, Astroquery, NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, SciPy, Pillow, and tools for accessing astronomical archive data through web and cloud interfaces.

The creative aspect of SKYWATCH 102 is its combination of scientific archive access and interactive visualization in one accessible platform. Rather than requiring users to manually inspect complex astronomical files, it provides a more approachable interface for exploring real NASA observations.

The project aims to encourage curiosity about infrared astronomy, improve public access to scientific data, and demonstrate how NASA mission observations can be transformed into interactive experiences for students, astronomy enthusiasts, and researchers.

AI-assisted tools were used during development for brainstorming, research, coding assistance, debugging, and technical troubleshooting. The project implementation and final results were reviewed by the development team.
